types.embedding_query_text: Company: An organization engaged in commercial, industrial, or professional activities. Also called Business, Corporation, Enterprise, Organization, Firm. Examples: Meta, Irregular, OpenAI, Anthropic.

chosen_type.label: Corporation
chosen_type.justification: Corporation is a legal entity formed for business purposes, aligning with the definition of 'Company' and examples like Meta and OpenAI.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: OnlineBusiness
candidates.comment: An OnlineBusiness is a particular business that operates primarily or entirely online. Also called e-business, internet business, digital enterprise. Examples: an e-commerce site, an online travel agency, a virtual doctor's office. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which has a physical presence.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

types.embedding_query_text: AIModel: An artificial intelligence system designed to perform specific tasks or mimic human behavior. Also called Artificial intelligence model, Machine learning model, AI system, Neural network model, Intelligent agent. Examples: Muse Spark model.

chosen_type.label: SoftwareApplication
chosen_type.justification: SoftwareApplication is a program for specific tasks, fitting the AIModel description and the example 'Muse Spark model' as an AI system.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: MathSolver
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a tool or application capable of solving a subset of mathematical problems. Also called mathematical calculator, problem solver, equation solver. Examples: an online algebra solver, a geometry calculator, a calculus problem-solving app.

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

candidates.label: SolveMathAction
candidates.comment: The action of taking a mathematical expression and directing users to a resource capable of solving or simplifying it. Also called math solving, equation solving, calculation action. Examples: entering '2+2' into a calculator app, inputting a complex equation into Wolfram Alpha, using a math solver website.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific point in time expressed numerically. Also called Temporal marker, Chronological point, Calendar date, Time reference, Day marker. Examples: 2026-08-06, 2026-07-30, Wednesday, last week.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.definition: A calendar date without time component, representing a temporal marker for events.
chosen_type.justification: Date represents a specific calendar date, matching the numerical format examples '2026-08-06' and '2026-07-30'.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: NewsOutlet: A media organization that produces and distributes news content. Also called Media company, News organization, Broadcast network, Publication, Journalistic outlet. Examples: The Information.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: NewsMediaOrganization produces and disseminates news, fitting the definition and example 'The Information' as a media outlet.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: AdvertiserContentArticle
candidates.comment: An AdvertiserContentArticle is an Article that has been paid for or produced to the specifications of an external entity. Also called sponsored article, advertorial, native advertising, paid content. Examples: A blog post promoting a product written by an influencer, a sponsored news segment, an article funded by a brand. Distinct from NewsArticle, which is typically produced by independent journalists.

types.embedding_query_text: Source Examples: A source familiar with the situation.

chosen_type.label: InformationSource
chosen_type.definition: An entity providing information or context for a situation, often as an anonymous or unnamed party.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits the concept of an anonymous source providing information, so a new subtype of Organization is minted.

mentions: A source familiar with the situation

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: ActionAccessSpecification
candidates.comment: An ActionAccessSpecification is an Intangible item detailing the requirements that must be met to perform a specific Action. Also called access requirements, action prerequisites, permission rules. Examples: "Requires login," "Subscription needed," "Age 18+," "Admin privileges."

candidates.label: BedDetails
candidates.comment: An Intangible entity providing specific information about the types and quantities of beds available in an accommodation. Also called bed configuration, sleeping arrangements, bed inventory. Examples: "Details for two twin beds and one king bed", "Information on a queen bed with a sofa bed", "Specifics for a bunk bed setup". Distinct from BedType, which is an enumeration of bed categories.

candidates.label: MedicalCause
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing the causative agent(s) responsible for a pathophysiologic process leading to a medical condition, symptom, or sign. Also called etiology, causative factor, underlying reason. Examples: "HIV virus" as a cause of AIDS, "pulmonary embolism" as a cause of cardiac arrest, "bacterial infection".

candidates.label: Quotation
candidates.comment: A Quotation is a CreativeWork representing a passage or statement, often from a written work, attributable to an author. Also called quote, excerpt, citation. Examples: "To be or not to be, that is the question.", a famous saying, a line from a movie, a passage from a book.
